newsitem.title: USA: Hilton CEO says $70 per share bid is firm.
newsitem.headline: Hilton CEO says $70 per share bid is firm.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach Wednesday said the company will not raise his company's $70 per share cash and stock offer for ITT Corp.
"We're taking our best shot," Bollenbach told Reuters. "We wanted to make a full bid. We wanted to make sure all the cards are on the table, and they are now."
Asked directly whether at any point he would raise the offer price, Bollenbach's reply was a flat "no."

Hilton launched its bid for ITT back in January at $55 per share. Since then, ITT has moved to block the bid, and in July it unveiled a plan to split into three companies, buy back some stock at $70 a share and restructure its debt.
Hilton has fallen under some criticism in financial markets for not raising its price sooner, but Bollenbach said he would not have done anything differently in the battle for ITT.

"When we made an offer for ITT, with a lot of good advice, we had a pretty clear picture of what the future would bring, and I can tell you we had no surprises," Bollenbach said. "We were patient, we stuck to our plan, I believe at the right time we've made our new offer."
He said the impetus to make the new bid now was that ITT's final strategy had been put on the table.
The next move is firmly in the hands of ITT's board and its shareholders, Bollenbach said.
Indeed, Hilton's present strategy is to lobby ITT's shareholders in order to force ITT management to call for a vote on Hilton's offer, and Bollenbach said initial results have been positive.
ITT has declined to comment on the offer except to say its board will review it.

In the event that merger talks with ITT management or a shareholder vote do not materialize, Hilton has filed a suit in U.S. District Court in Nevada asking the court to force a vote. In previous legal battles surrounding its ITT bid, however, Hilton has been unsuccessful.

Lastly, Bollenbach said it will not walk away from the takeover battle until ITT is successful in breaking up the company and forming ITT Destinations with a staggered board. ITT Destinations would be the owner of ITT's Sheraton hotels and Caesars casinos. ITT expects that spin-off to take place this fall.
"They have to come and work with us before they do that spin-out," he said.
